basis.governing_question: Why do property and health claims take too long to settle, and what claims operating model should Atlântico Seguros move to?

phases.name: Diagnostic
phases.objective_one_line: Establish where and why property and health claims lose time compared with the improved motor process.

gate.label: Findings sign-off
gate.decision: Accept the diagnostic findings as the basis for the design phase?

phases.name: Design
phases.objective_one_line: Define the claims operating model to move to and the plan to get there.

gate.label: Final readout
gate.decision: Approve the recommendations and presentation to take to the Board?

workstreams.name: Claims process baseline
workstreams.answers: How do property and health claims move from notice to settlement, and where does time build up?
activities: Map the steps of property and health claims
Analyze handling times in operational claims data
Compare handling steps with the improved motor process

workstreams.name: Claims handling pain points
workstreams.answers: What do the people who handle claims see as the causes of delay?
activities: Interview claims handlers and team leads
Interview the COO and the Head of Claims
Review files of delayed property and health claims

workstreams.name: Settlement and satisfaction
workstreams.answers: How long do property and health claims take to settle today, how satisfied are customers, and what drives delay most?
activities: Measure settlement time by claim type from claims data
Rank causes of delay by their effect on settlement time

workstreams.name: Target claims model options
workstreams.answers: Which claims operating models could cut settlement time without lowering customer satisfaction?
activities: Define candidate claims operating models from the diagnostic
Keep options within the existing claims IT system
Compare options against the two success criteria

workstreams.name: Design of the chosen model
workstreams.answers: How will claims, roles and handoffs work in the chosen model for property and health claims?
activities: Detail process steps, roles and decision rights
Work through the design with claims handlers
Define how settlement time and satisfaction are tracked

workstreams.name: Recommendation and roadmap
workstreams.answers: What will the chosen model do to settlement time and satisfaction, and how does the client move to it?
activities: Test the chosen model against the success criteria
Plan the transition steps and change actions
Prepare the written report and board presentation

deliverables.name: Property and health claims process baseline
Interview synthesis of claims pain points
Detailed design of the chosen claims model
Written report and board presentation on the claims model

events.label: Kick-off
events.purpose: Align scope, plan and access to claims data
events.decision: Confirm the scope, plan and access to claims data?
agenda: Present the engagement scope and plan
Align on interview and data access
Confirm steering roles and meeting dates

events.label: Check-in: early findings
events.purpose: Review early process and interview findings
events.decision: Confirm where the diagnostic should focus in the remaining weeks?
agenda: Review pain points from the interviews
Confirm the focus for the remaining diagnostic

events.label: Findings sign-off
events.decision: Accept the diagnostic findings as the basis for the design phase?
agenda: Present the baseline and the prioritized causes of delay
Discuss what the findings mean for the target model
Decide whether the findings are accepted

events.label: Workshop: model options
events.purpose: Review options and pick the preferred model
events.decision: Which target model should be detailed for the final recommendation?
agenda: Present the target claims model options
Review the options against the success criteria

events.label: Final readout
events.purpose: Approve the recommendations for the Board
events.decision: Approve the recommendations and presentation to take to the Board?
agenda: Present the report and the board presentation
Review the detailed design and transition roadmap
Confirm the recommendations to take to the Board

deadline.text: Recommendations presented to the Board on March 15, 2027

architect_notes: Engagement length is not stated; the Diagnostic (5-7 weeks) and Design (7-9 weeks) lengths are estimates that fit the 19 weeks available.
Not covered by the phases: ASF, supervisor guidance on claims-handling response times. Confirm whether it is in scope.
Replacing the claims IT system is out of scope; model options are designed around the current system, which may limit some options.
Rollout of the chosen claims model is not in these phases; the plan ends at the transition roadmap.
